results.raw_content: [Back to Search Programs](/search) # Master Informatique — E-services [Université de Lille](/university/universite-de-lille) Ronchin, France2 yearsTaught in FrenchOpen to international students ## About Master Informatique — E-services At Université de Lille, tuition comes to 250 EUR per year. E-services is a specialization within the Master Informatique at Université de Lille, in Villeneuve D'Ascq, France. This track within computer science focuses on the design, development, and delivery of digital services over networks, covering subjects such as web application development, service-oriented architecture, distributed systems, and the technologies used to build and operate online services accessed by users and other systems. Students typically study programming, web technologies, software architecture, and the methods used to design services that are reliable, secure, and able to scale to many users. Graduates from this kind of program commonly move into roles such as web developer, software engineer specializing in service-based architectures, IT consultant, or positions within companies that build and operate digital platforms and online services. The broad coverage of service design and web technology also supports careers in sectors where digital service delivery is central, including e-commerce, telecommunications, and public digital services. The program spans two years and leads to a master's degree, taught in French, so applicants should have a solid command of the language for technical and programming-focused coursework. The academic year begins in September. Yearly tuition is 250 EUR, in line with fees at French public universities. Students interested in building and operating digital services accessed over networks may find this specialization at Université de Lille a relevant route into that area of software development. results.raw_content: Formations en Informatique de Lille Portail pédagogique [![accueil FIL](css/trans.gif)](https://portail.fil.univ-lille.fr "FIL") [L1 Maths-Info](index.php?dipl=L1_MI) [Licence Info](index.php?dipl=L) [Master Info](index.php?dipl=MInfo) [Master Miage](index.php?dipl=MMiage) [Master BioInfo](index.php?dipl=M1MISO) [Master DS](index.php?dipl=MDS) [Alternance](index.php?dipl=Alternance) [General Information](index.php?dipl=MDS&sem=MDSinfo&ue=ACCUEIL) [M1](index.php?dipl=MDS&sem=M1DS&ue=ACCUEIL) [M2](index.php?dipl=MDS&sem=M2DS&ue=ACCUEIL) Vous êtes ici : [FIL](https://sciences-technologies.univ-lille.fr/informatique/) > [Portail](index.php) > [Master DS](index.php?dipl=MDS) > [M1](index.php?dipl=MDS&sem=M1DS&ue=ACCUEIL) [Presentation](#) [Applying](#) [Courses](#) [Internship](#) ## Aims of the first year of the Master The major goal of the first year of the Master is to provide students with: * the scientific background required to master machine learning at a high level: mathematics (calculus, algebra, optimization, probabilities, statistics), computer science (algorithms, analysis of algorithms, databases), signal processing, * the fundamentals of machine learning: supervised and unsupervised machine learning models, evaluation of machine learning models, neural networks, decision theory, etc. The first year of the master mixes up theory and practice. Each course offers both theoretical lectures and exercise or lab sessions where students learn how to apply the theoretical content of the lectures in practice. The practice of machine learning is emphasized through a one-week data challenge and a final internship in a company or an academic lab. In their first year, students are also initiated to research in machine learning through regular seminars given by researchers and practitioners in the field, and through a research project spread over 5 months in one of the research labs of University of Lille, Centrale Lille, or IMT Nord Europe. ## Who can apply? The M1 in data science is open to students who have completed (or will have completed by the end of the academic year) a Bachelor / Licence (or an equivalent degree) in one of the following fields: * Pure or applied mathematics, * Computer science, * Mathematics and computer science, * Mathematics and computer science applied to social science (French MIASHS programme), * Electrical engineering, * Computer engineering, * or any other Bachelor degree with a strong curriculum in maths and computer science. Students who are currently enrolled in post-graduate studies (Master programme or Engineering school) can still apply as long as they hold a Bachelor in one of the aforementioned fields. Applicants must demonstrate proficiency in English at the CEFR level B2 or above. Your level in English can be demonstrated in several ways: by an official certificate (TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, etc.) or through a statement issued by your university indicating your level on the CEFR scale (B2, C1, etc.). ## Important dates **Applications through Mon Master:** The dates for the 2027 application process are not public yet. The application period should typically start around February 2027. **Applications through Études en France:** Applications should be sent from October to December 2026, to apply for the 2027-2028 academic year. Please contact your local Campus France office to know the specific deadlines that apply yo you (see the list of Campus France offices [here](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/espaces)). ## How to apply? The application process depends on your nationality, the country in which you are currently living, and whether you apply as a full-time student or through the Erasmus programme. ### French / EU students French and EU students, as well as students currently living in France or the EU (regardless of their nationalities), must apply through the national platform: [Mon Master](https://www.monmaster.gouv.fr/master/universite-de-lille-epe/science-des-donnees-1?q=data%20science%20lille&position=0&layout=1). Please note that the Master in Data science is referenced twice on MonMaster: under Université de Lille, and under Centrale Lille; you must apply through the [page of Université de Lille](https://www.monmaster.gouv.fr/master/universite-de-lille-epe/science-des-donnees-1?q=data%20science%20lille&position=0&layout=1) only. ### Foreign students (outside of the EU) If you are currently enrolled in a higher education institution in France or in the EU, you must use the same procedure as French / EU students (please see above). If you are currently living in one of the countries listed under the Campus France procedure [Études en France](https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/etudesenfrance/), you must follow the specific procedure of Campus France. Please refer to the [Études en France website](https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/etudesenfrance/) to check if you qualify for their procedure and access the detailed application process. Please note that the Études en France process starts very early on: the process to join the Master at year N typically starts during the first semester (usually in October) of the year N-1. **Important note:** You may find two distinct pages on Études en France for the Master in Data science: one to apply to University of Lille, the other to apply to Centrale Lille. While this is the same Master program, **you must apply through University of Lille only** (not Centrale Lille), otherwise your application will not be processed. If you do not qualify for the Études en France procedure, you must follow the same application procedure as French/EU students (please see above). ### Erasmus students If you want to attend classes in the Master through the Erasmus programme, you should follow the Erasmus procedure of your home university and list courses of the Master in your learning agreement. The adminitrative staff of your university will send us your application file directly. ## What documents should I provide to apply? Applicants must provide the following documents with their application: * A curriculum vitae * Transcripts of grades of your current and previous higher education programmes * A cover letter (lettre de motivation) * One or several documents attesting your level in English Additional documents may be required depending on the procedure through which you are applying. Optionally, applicants can provide some of the following documents: * Recommandation letters * Official certificate of proficiency in English (TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, etc.) * Statement of proficiency in English issued by your university ## M1: 1st year, 1st (fall / M1S1) semester and 2nd (spring / M1S2) semester All courses take place over 24 hours. Two refresher courses are proposed in computer science and mathematics to help students who would need some upgrade to attend the program in good conditions; taking at least one of them is mandatory and decided by the teaching team based on the student's background. Students can always choose to attend both. A complete description of all courses of the first year (M1) is available [here](https://nextcloud.univ-lille.fr/index.php/s/dtoSkMp9kbQ7GBj/download). ### Courses of the first (fall) semester | Name | Status | Teaching hours | Credits (ECTS) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Refresher in mathematics | Optional | 24 | 3 | | Refresher in computer science | Optional | 24 | | Python and tools for research | Mandatory | 24 | | Fundamental notions of mathematics | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Probability 1 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Statistics 1 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Algorithms and their complexity 1 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Data bases 1 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Machine learning 1: Hands on! | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Machine learning 2: The landscape of machine learning | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Ethics & law: Legal aspects of data analysis | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | English | Optional | 24 | 3 | | Foreign language (other than English) | Optional | 24 | | French for foreign students | Optional | 24 | ### Courses of the second (spring) semester | Name | Status | Teaching hours | Credits (ECTS) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Probability 2: Markov chains & processes | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Statistics 2: Introduction to estimation | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Optimization and numerical analysis | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Algorithms & their complexity 2 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Machine learning 3: Deep learning | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Models for machine learning | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Signal processing & functional data analysis | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Data challenge | Mandatory | 1 week | 3 | | Research project | Mandatory | 3 | | Seminars | Mandatory | | Internship | Mandatory | 6+ weeks | 3 | ## First year internship ### General information The internship of the first year is mandatory and must last at least 6 weeks. The typical duration is three to four months. It can be done in an academic lab of a company, in France or in a Foreign country. The topic of the internship must be related to the field of data science, in a broad sense. Eligible topics include: * Design, deployement, or experimental validation of machine learning models * Software development related to data management, data analysis, or machine learning * Database design, management, or * Mathematical modeling At the end of the internship, students must validate the internship through a memoir and a defense. ### Funding during the internship Under French regulations, the employer must provide a compensation to interns if the duration of the internship is 2 months or more. The minimum rate for the compensation is 4.05€/hour; many companies offer more. Students doing their internship abroad can apply for a mobility grant from the Graduate programme IKS or the Sherlock IA chair. The amount of the grant depends on the conditions of the internship. Calls for applications are sent to the students during the academic year. ### Examples of M1 Internships * Cloud shadow removal in sun observations, LIS, University of Toulon (Toulon, France) * Information extraction from legal documents, Lexis Nexis (Paris, France) * Implementation and assessment of function secret sharing algorithms, INRIA (Lille, France) * 3D detection of vulnerable road users, IMT Nord Europe (Lille, France)

This Master’s program is a natural next step for students who have earned a general Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science. The program offers four specialized tracks spread over two years, allowing students to deepen their expertise in current fields. Upon completion of a final-year internship, graduates from each track can either enter the workforce in engineering roles or pursue a Ph.D. to develop international expertise. [Read more](#) ## Objectives The Master's in Computer Science aims to train high-level professionals and researchers capable of responding to current and future technological challenges: artificial intelligence, big data, cybersecurity, distributed systems, human-machine interaction, high-performance computing, etc. [Read more](#) ## Know-how and skills *Cybersecurity Track*: From the Edge to the Cloud: Working closely with major players in cloud computing (who have a strong presence in our region), particularly their services and CISO teams, while also engaging with cybersecurity firms, the Cybersecurity Master’s program: From Edge to Cloud provides students with cutting-edge knowledge and skills in the fields of IT security, cloud software design and deployment, as well as the management and maintenance of large data centers. The program also emphasizes technology monitoring skills, which are essential for security specialists. In addition to skills in cybersecurity, systems, and system architecture, the Cybersecurity: From Edge to Cloud program equips students with broad competencies in computer science and software development. *Computer Science Track*: In this track, depending on the specialization chosen by the student, they will develop the skills associated with either the Cybersecurity track: from edge to cloud, the AI track, or the GL track. *AI Track:* The skills acquired in this AI track are primarily related to artificial intelligence techniques for the exploitation, analysis, and forecasting of large datasets. The curriculum focuses on three pillars: machine learning, algorithms, and databases. Upon completion of the master’s program, students will participate in the design and implementation of solutions based on supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning; advanced databases beyond the relational model and SQL; optimization methods central to learning; and data mining and deep learning techniques using textual or networked data. The program is complemented by skills that enable students to integrate into a team and understand the key principles of entrepreneurship in computer science. The role of research initiation in the master’s program is essential in this field. *Software Engineering Track*: Working closely with the business, research, and innovation sectors, students in the *Software* Engineering track acquire knowledge and skills applicable to the development and maintenance of modern information systems. In addition, an awareness of technology trends facilitates the transition to the integration and effective deployment of new software technologies. The skills acquired in the Software Engineering track are as follows: mastering the concepts and tools of software development; being able to contribute to all stages of the application lifecycle; knowing how to adopt a development process that ensures the production of high-performance, quality software; knowing how to effectively manage a development team; mastering leading-edge technologies while being able to adapt to those that will replace them; being able to integrate into an agile team; understanding the key principles of entrepreneurship. [Read more](#) ## International dimension The Computer Science program is open to international students and is taught in English. Students have the option to spend a semester or a year studying abroad. [Read more](#) ## Training benefits * Strong background in computer science and software development. * Training focused on openness: * These tracks are open to all specializations within the master's program: cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and software engineering. * Openness to research and innovation: events, projects, and courses related to research. These include RIC (Research, Innovation, and Creativity) Day and meetings with members of the CRIStAL, INRIA, and IRCICA laboratories. This awareness of research enables students to pursue their studies at doctoral level and also, in an industrial context, to understand technological developments during their careers in order to contribute to their companies' strategic thinking. Possibility of pursuing doctoral studies. * International opportunities: Students can spend a semester or a year studying at a foreign university. * Openness to the business world: more than 100 work-study students, strong interaction with the professional world (internships, work-study programs), courses introducing students to the business world. High employability upon completion of training. Professional networks, between internships and support: support in discovering professions and finding internships; three- to six-month internships during the master's program; presentations by numerous IT specialists from companies in the Lille metropolitan area. * Training accessible to as many people as possible: 750 students enrolled in the department, low tuition fees. * High-quality learning environment: 450 high-quality workstations at your disposal, and nearly 60 dedicated faculty members committed to your success. [Read more](#) ## Organization The training is organized around the following skill sets: BCC - Building your career plan and developing cross-disciplinary skills useful for the IT sector BCC - Mobilizing the theoretical foundations of computer science BCC – Analyzing IT system vulnerabilities and developing secure solutions BCC - Designing and developing software by mastering the life cycle and associated methods BCC - Implementing artificial intelligence models to model and solve complex problems [Read more](#) ## Open on a sandwich basis | | | | --- | --- | | Type of contract | Professional training contract, Apprenticeship contract | [Read more](#) [Read more](#) ## Courses | | | | --- | --- | | Internship | Mandatory | [Read more](#) ## Program ### Select a program ### Computer Sciences The **Master's program in Computer Science** at the University of Lille offers cutting-edge training for students aiming for management positions in the information science and communications technology sector. This Master's degree is a natural continuation of studies for students with a Bachelor's degree in General Computer Science. This program offers four specializations spread over two years, allowing students to deepen their skills in current fields. After completing an end-of-studies internship, graduates from each track can either enter the professional world in engineering positions or pursue a PhD and develop international expertise. [View the full page for this track](/fr/offre-de-formation/master-lmd-XB/master-informatique-MG001981/computer-sciences-MX195387.html) ### Cybersecurity: from edge to cloud The University of Lille’s **Master’s program in Computer Science** offers cutting-edge training for students aiming for executive positions in the fields of information science and communication technologies. This Master’s program is a natural next step for students holding a general Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science. The program offers four specialized tracks spanning two years, allowing students to deepen their expertise in current fields of interest. Upon completion of a final-year internship, graduates from each track can either enter the workforce in engineering roles or pursue a Ph.D. to develop international expertise. [View the full page for this track](/fr/offre-de-formation/master-lmd-XB/master-informatique-MG001981/cybersecurite-du-edge-au-cloud-MX195390.html) ### Software engineering The **Software Engineering track** focuses on the design and development of agile software—that is, applications whose features are perfectly aligned with user needs. The program therefore combines methods, concepts, and technologies to foster the creation of innovative applications without ever losing sight of efficiency. The application areas covered range from embedded computing to large distributed systems. [View the full page for this track](/fr/offre-de-formation/master-lmd-XB/master-informatique-MG001981/genie-logiciel-MX002037.html) ### Artificial intelligence Machine learning is now at the heart of the artificial intelligence technologies that are increasingly permeating our daily lives. This evolution is profoundly transforming traditional information systems and raising new challenges in data management and analysis. Understanding how to collect and organize data and scale up to handle very large volumes—but above all, understanding, comparing, and evaluating new machine learning algorithms—are among these challenges. These are the objectives of **the AI track**, which is unique in that it develops both advanced fundamental scientific knowledge and advanced technical skills—qualities essential for understanding the rapid changes in a field that is still maturing. Designed for careers in data science, big data, machine learning, and artificial intelligence, the Machine Learning track offers a solid foundation in computer science. The proposed program reflects a clear commitment to prioritizing development skills that are firmly grounded in solid theoretical knowledge of machine learning, algorithms, and databases.
